newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Even UK said sympathetic to ending EU veto misuse.
newsitem.headline: Even UK said sympathetic to ending EU veto misuse.

text.p: Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo said on Tuesday that most countries in the European Union were now willing to give up the national veto in foreign policy matters and that even Britain was understanding about the idea.
"The will to get away from the tyranny of the veto is more or less there, even in the U.K.," van Mierlo told a European Parliament committee.

Britain's Conservative government is vehemently opposed to any further loss of the veto in EU decision making and has pledged to block any move in that direction during the inter-governmental conference (IGC).
But van Mierlo said that the misuse of unanimity -- which has included cases of single countries disrupting relations with non-EU countries -- was weighing on everyone in the bloc.
"People there (Britain) are not insensitive to the idea that there are limits," he said.
The EU is aiming to complete the IGC by the end of the Dutch presidency, in June.

Van Mierlo said he believed negotiations were moving along and that there would be some progress shown next month when EU foreign ministers meet in Italy to celebrate the 40th anniversary of the Treaty of Rome.
"We hope by that time we will be at least half way to getting a full first draft of a treaty," he said.
